assumptions: Source assumption: dividends grow at a constant rate g forever with valuation in discrete steps and next-period dividend D1 (geometric-series derivation shown in the article).
Application profile: stable-growth firm (regulated utility, large financial firm, REIT) with required return k above g, both per-annum decimals.
k and g sit on the same price basis, and the inflation assumption is consistent with the valuation currency (Damodaran basic premise).

gaps: Needs new quantity meanings: expected_dividend, required_return, growth_rate; output reuses the existing present_value meaning. No current-runtime projection attempted.
The Damodaran r notation and the article k notation denote the same required-return quantity; alias recorded here, not as separate meanings.

models.inverse_notes: k=D1/P0+g needs P0>0 and g>=0; checked ConEd: 2.142/41.80+0.05=0.10124 against published 0.1013 (rounding). g=k-D1/P0 under the same conditions; D1=P0*(k-g) needs k>g. Admitted boundary: D1=0 gives P0=0 (no distributions). The limit k-to-g from above is a blow-up, never an admissible equality, and the guard excludes it.
limitations: Short-run supernormal growth needs the explicitly separate two-stage DDM, not this expression.
The value is hypersensitive to (k-g) near the guard; the guard excludes equality but near-guard inputs remain economically fragile.
Perpetual growth above the economy nominal growth rate is inadmissible (Damodaran caps it near nominal GNP); that macro ceiling is textual, not an executable predicate.

references.method: Damodaran computes DPS1=2.04*1.05=2.142 and Value=2.142/(0.1013-0.05)=$41.80 with cost of equity 6%+0.75*5.5%=10.13%; recomputation gives 41.754, so tolerance covers the rounded inputs and $0.01 output rounding.
references.provenance: Published worked example (Con Edison, January 1996) in Damodaran NYU Stern lecture notes, Stable Growth DDM section

limitations: The linear approximation rreal ~= inom-f holds only for rates near zero; reference b quantifies the neglected-product gap (rreal*f=0.00146).
Expected versus realized inflation (forecast error, indexed-bond basis) is outside this identity.
Negative nominal rates are outside the tested scope.
